Subject: Tempo buffer allocation & eviction schedule for Dedicated commit (AzureTech)

Marta — following up on last week's call. We sketched two mechanisms for handling transient spikes on Dedicated pools tied to the AzureTech commit: a tempo-buffer (short-lived reserved slab) and a measured eviction schedule when we hit sustained saturation.

High-level asks for procurement/ops alignment: 
- Could you confirm the expected daily 95th percentile token throughput during peak test windows? (Kevin mentioned an internal stress test next month.)
- Are there specific blackout windows (maintenance/backup) where you prefer no prewarm allocation?

What we propose in brief (attachments contain numbers):
1) Tempo Buffer: a small reserved slab (e.g., 8 GPUs) for 30–90 minute bursts tied to a crediting budget that resets hourly.
2) Eviction + Fallback: when buffer consumed for >90 minutes, pre-configured eviction rules will reclaim ephemeral workloads first and route critical traffic to a slightly lower-capacity model variant.
3) Canary & Telemetry: 5-minute telemetry hooks and a canary route to ensure model fallbacks don't regress latency beyond SLA.

Ben, Laura — can you review the attached capacity model and proposed eviction script? I want numbers we can hand to procurement.

Marta / Procurement — we can turn this into a clause in the Dedicated amendment (tempo-burst credits, eviction SLA, and required telemetry) once we align on sizing and blackout windows.

Thanks,
Karthik
Sr. Director, Capacity Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Karthik / Laura — quick tech notes after reviewing the capacity sheet. Quoting Marta for context.

On Thu, Dec 5, 2029 at 11:02 AM Marta Ruiz <marta@azuretech.com> wrote:
> - 95th pct token throughput ... 1.2M tokens/min (peak windows run 60–90 minutes).

Our take:
- If AzureTech's peaks are 60–90 minutes, a 30–90 minute tempo buffer is fine for short shocks but you'll want an escalation policy for mid-length peaks (45–180 minutes).
- Suggested guardbands: 8 GPU tempo slab for immediate spikes; a configurable shoulder pool of 16 GPUs that can be auto-unlocked if the tempo slab remains saturated for more than 45 minutes and telemetry shows sustained qps above threshold. Shoulder pool activation should require both a telemetry threshold and an approval flag (ops webhook) to avoid accidental cost overruns.
- Credit accounting: we recommend per-GPU-minute billing for tempo buffer active time, with an overage flag if shoulder pool activation occurs (mapped to a separate mRR bucket). That maps cleanly to committed mRR + burst credits.

I attached a short pseudocode evacuation sequence to the capacity sheet. Laura — can you confirm the latency tradeoffs for the model variant fallback? If fallback adds +30–80ms p95 we need to list that in the SLA addendum.

Ben
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Marta / team — following up on Ben's points. A few specifics for the SLA language and telemetry hooks: 

- Telemetry: we require 1-min granularity for GPU utilization, queue depth, and p95 latency for both the primary and fallback model routes. These are necessary for automatic shoulder activation to trigger reliably.
- Eviction order (recommended):
  1) Ephemeral preemptible dev workloads (tagged dev:*),
  2) Non-latency-sensitive batch jobs (batch:*),
  3) Ephemeral tempo slab (if still under pressure),
  4) Model-fallback activation (route to smaller/quantized variant).
- Blackout: we will ensure control-plane operations avoid activation during your 0200–0300 UTC backup; the system will queue activation requests until 0300 UTC unless marked emergency.

I'll add a short section for expected p95 delta on fallback; early sims show +45ms p95 on quantized variant at your target sequence length. I'll include that in the next revision of the PDF.

Laura
Director, Product Ops — Redwood Console

Marta / Procurement — attached is an updated one-page summary reflecting Ben and Laura's inputs. Key commercial mapping: 

- Tempo buffer pricing: billed per-GPU-minute while active (line item on invoice). Example: 8 GPU slab active for 45 minutes consumes 360 GPU-minutes charged against burst credits or billed as overage if credits exhausted.
- Shoulder pool: conditional activation with ops webhook approval; billed as a separate reserved burst SKU with predefined mRR uplift if used beyond 3 activations/month.
- Eviction & fallback: documented ordinal eviction, automatic fallback route, and p95 delta disclosed in SLA addendum.

Next steps we propose: 
1) Procurement — confirm you are OK with per-GPU-minute billing for tempo buffer and the monthly activation cap on shoulder pool that triggers an mRR uplift.
2) Ops (Kevin) — confirm eviction preference and whether you want shoulder auto-approval turned on for an initial 30-day pilot.
3) Legal — we'll prepare a short amendment for the Dedicated agreement that includes tempo-burst credits, metrics required, blackout windows, and telemetry obligations.

If we get agreement, we'll produce a numbered amendment for signature (DocuSign link in related links).

Thanks all,
Karthik
